*Year 4 of the Ouka Era—the 7th of July.*
Rimu: "Hmmm... Mmmmmm."
Shimei: "......"
Rimu: "Hmmmmm... That's it! I just don't get it!"
Shimei: "I guess this job just isn't for you, Rimu."
Rimu: "Ugh! I can't do it, I just can't!"
Rimu: "It's so boring, it's driving me crazy!"
Shimei: "I don't think clerical work is all that menial, though..."
Rimu: "Speaking of which, why do you have to work on your day off, anyway?"
Shimei: "Huh...? Well..."
Koume: "Kondo-ojisama, I finished filing these documents."
Kondo: "Oh, thank you. You're so quick at picking things up, Koume, it's a huge help. Please handle these documents next."
Koume: "Yes sir, please leave it to me."
*After that incident, Koume really did become a clerk for the Nakamachi magistrate's office.*
*Not only does she pick things up quickly, but she's become extremely proficient and is single-handedly responsible for the financial and clerical work.*
*Of course, I'm not sure if she actually likes the work or if she just likes being relied on...*
*But she's always doing paperwork and filing documents regardless of whether it's a holiday or not.*
Shimei: "I can't really slack off when Koume is working so hard."
Rimu: "...That's the kind of logic they use in a sweatshop, y'know."
Kondo: "Why don't you take a break, Koume-kun? You two should take one too, you both look worn out."
Koume: "...? Yes, sir, I will do so."
Rimu: "Hey, Koume-chan, do you like paper?"
Koume: "I do, and I like to read the writing, but I like reading books the most."
Shimei: "Why would you ask that?"
Rimu: "I figured, if she likes paper, maybe that's why she's so happy to file documents."
Shimei: "By that logic, you should like organizing iron and lumber, Rimu."
Kondo: "Well, we have boxes made out of wood... maybe you'd like to organize those?"
Rimu: "Erk... I don't like the sound of that..."
Rimu: "Today is my day off and I'm gonna do what I want! Which means I'm going back to my room!"
Shimei: "Ah..."
*Rimu practically sprints out of the office, quick as she can, without waiting for a response.*
Kondo: "Well, I wasn't going to say anything around Hiraga-kun, but you should learn to take it easy too, Koume-kun."
Koume: "Learn to take it easy?"
Kondo: "You've been working yourself non-stop this past month."
Koume: "That is what I want, though. Is... Is that a problem?"
Kondo: "No, not at all, but resting sometimes is also part of your job. In that case, Shimei-kun..."
Shimei: "Yes?"
Kondo: "I want you to show Koume-kun how to spend her time off."
Shimei: "How to spend her time off?"
Kondo: "Essentially, even if you aren't physically fatigued, you still accumulate mental fatigue."
Kondo: "Ahh... Ultimately, I'm saying you're free to do as you like. I leave the rest up to you, Shimei-kun."
Shimei: "I feel like that's easier said than done..."
Kondo: "On that note, I should be enjoying my time off as well. See you later."
*With that, Kondo-san left the office with a leisurely wave.*
*Koume and I are the only ones remaining...*
Koume: "So, umm... What should I do...?"
Shimei: "Well, let's help you learn how to spend a day off."
Koume: "My time off... All right! I will do my best to learn how to relax!"
*You might find it's easier if you, uhh... turn the energy down a notch.*
Koume: "..."
Shimei: "Okay, first, I need you to come with me. I'll explain the rest after that!"
Koume: "Okay!"
Koume: "Huh? What are those voices...?"
*We could hear the reverberating voices of training from the dojo.*
Shimei: "Sounds like Hijikata and the others are sparring."
Koume: "So... Have Hijikata-san and the others been training in the dojo since morning?"
Shimei: "I guess so."
*If he was free, I'd been hoping he would help me out here.*
Koume: "But, is training any different from work?"
Shimei: "While it's all basically the same thing to the Shinsengumi, I think it's somewhat different."
Shimei: "If they don't train every day, they'll get weaker... you could say it's like studying for their bodies."
Koume: "Studying for your body...? Sakura-oneesama said she would be training as well."
Shimei: "Actually, that reminds me. Toyama said she would be training with the Shinsengumi starting today."
Koume: "Does that mean that she will be studying with them? Which means, which means..."
Shimei: "We probably shouldn't bother them..."
Koume: "So exciting..."
Shimei: "...Do you want to go watch them train?"
Koume: "Yes, please! I would love to!"
Sakura: "......"
Okita: "......"
*We enter the dojo to find Toyama and Okita facing off with wooden swords.*
*Hijikata, who has been watching their bout with a serious look, notices our arrival.*
Hijikata: "Oh, now this is an unusual sight. I didn't expect to see you here, Shimei-kun—let alone Koume-chan!"
Koume: "I wanted to see what training was like..."
Koume: "W-Would we be in the way?"
Hijikata: "Not at all. If they get distracted just by you being here, it'll just mean they still need more practice."
*Hijikata is right. Okita and Toyama continue to stare each other down, making no indication they've noticed our presence.*
Koume: "Sakura-oneesama and Okita-neesama are just standing there quietly... What are they doing?"
Hijikata: "Toyama is measuring things up to see if there might be any openings to strike. Okita is... doing what she always does."
Koume: "What she always does?"
Hijikata: "Well, you'll see."
*Toyama braces herself against Okita without presenting a single opening.*
*In contrast, Okita just stands there with her wooden sword up, looking otherwise just as relaxed as usual.*
*Okita fixes her gaze forward without making the slightest movement, as if she's letting Toyama's energy wash over and around her.*
*Okita seems full of openings while Toyama looks fully prepared...*
Shimei: (If she strikes, the match will just be over instantly, won't it?)
*Almost before I can finish the thought—*
Sakura: "Hyah!!!"
*Toyama draws her wooden sword and springs at Okita, putting her weight behind the blow.*
Okita: "......"
*But in that instant...*
Sakura: "...Urgh...!"
*Toyama's sword is gone from her hand. Okita's sword-point is at her prey's throat.*
Okita: "......"
Koume: "A-Amazing..."
Sakura: "...My loss."
Okita: "Hijikata, you're next..."
Hijikata: "All right! I'm gonna beat you this time!"
*Trading places with Toyama, Hijikata faces off against Okita.*
Sakura: "Dammit, what a humiliating spectacle that was."
Shimei: "I didn't think so."
Sakura: "Like hell. I didn't stand a chance, couldn't you tell?"
Sakura: "And you, Koume, just watching us train can't be all that interesting to you. Why are you here?"
Koume: "W-Well... I wanted to see what training was like, just this once."
Koume: "I-Is that a bad thing...?"
Sakura: "...Hmph. I don't really care, but I don't think you'll get anything out of it."
Koume: "That's not..."
Hijikata: "...I-I lost."
Shimei: "W-What? When did you lose, Hijikata?"
Hijikata: "Just now. I couldn't get in a single hit."
Hijikata: "What the heck am I doing wrong?"
Okita: "...Everything."
Hijikata: "C-Come on... That's harsh, Okita."
Okita: "Time is up. That's enough practice for today."
*Okita briskly leaves the dojo.*
Sakura: "I never thought there would be this much of a difference in my first joint practice with them."
Koume: "Is Okita-neesama really that strong?"
Sakura: "So strong I can't even learn anything from her. Honestly, it's done a number on my self-confidence."
Shimei: "Everything happened too fast to follow when we made the arrest, but seeing it up close now, she's pretty amazing."
Hijikata: "No one in the Shinsengumi compares to her. That's how overwhelming she is."
Koume: "Do you... Think I could do it too?"
Hijikata: "By that... Do you mean you want to try swordsmanship?"
Koume: "Yes, since I finally got the chance to observe it... That is, just a bit."
Sakura: "There's no way."
Shimei: "Y-You don't have to put it so bluntly."
Sakura: "I won't stop you if you insist on doing it, but it would be a waste of time."
Shimei: "How can you be so sure?"
Sakura: "Even the wooden swords are considerably heavy. Koume's more delicate frame wouldn't be able to handle one."
Koume: "I see... But you looked really incredible when you were training, Sakura-oneesama."
Koume: "What can I do to be more like you?"
Sakura: "L-Like me...?"
Hijikata: "Why don't you at least just try and show her? You said she's free to try it, right?"
Sakura: "T-That's true, I did, but..."
Koume: "...Can I?"
Sakura: "...F-Fine then."
Sakura: "Okay, come here. I'll show you the basic forms first."
Koume: "Yay! Thank you so much, Sakura-oneesama!"
*Toyama positions herself behind Koume and helps her take hold of the wooden sword, covering Koume's hands with her own.*
Shimei: "So much for rest and relaxation..."
*But I guess this is one way to spend a day off.*
Hijikata: "They're probably going to be a while. Shimei, wanna go grab a cup of tea?"
Shimei: "All right then."
*Hijikata and I exit the dojo, leaving the pair of them awkwardly training together.*
Shimei: "I never expected Koume to say she wanted to try training herself."
Hijikata: "I bet that it's a lot less about the sword and more about how much she idolizes and admires Sakura."
Hijikata: "She's gallant, honorable, and physically strong, not to mention brilliant."
Hijikata: "I can see how even a girl'd fall for that."
Shimei: "She also has a way with words."
Hijikata: "Hahaha. She even seems more manly than you sometimes."
Shimei: "Y-Yeah... maybe she does..."
Hijikata: "Come on, aren't you even gonna deny—huh?"
Rimu: "Ah! What are you two up to?"
Shimei: "We were just on our way to have some tea."
Rimu: "Oh really? So that means you're free then, right? Right?"
Hijikata: "...You're up to something, aren't you?"
Rimu: "Up to something? Who, me? I have no clue what you mean, no clue at all."
Shimei: "You made another contraption, didn't you?"
Rimu: "Bingo! Well done, Shimei-kun!"
Hijikata: "Hey, Shimei! Don't jinx us!"
Shimei: "Haha... It wouldn't be anything else, though."
Rimu: "But my machine this time is completely different! Wanna test it out?"
Shimei: "Test it out? I really don't expect that to end well."
Rimu: "Oh, come on! It'll be fine, it'll be fine!"
*Not bothering to listen, Rimu starts fiddling with something in a large box.*
Hijikata: "I won't forget you, Shimei. See ya!"
Shimei: "Aaaahhh! Don't leave me here! You coward!"
Rimu: "Shimei-kun! Here!"
Shimei: "Wah!"
*Ropes of various sizes spring from the box in Rimu's hands...*
Shimei: "Erk!"
*One loop gets around my foot, and I go down in a heap.*
Rimu: "Oooh, that caught you pretty good!"
Shimei: "I-I guess this will come in handy when catching someone who's trying to escape..."
Rimu: "The problem is the size and weight of the box."
Rimu: "Carrying this around normally would be difficult, I'll have to tweak that."
Shimei: "That thing is obviously dangerous. Nobody will go anywhere near you if you carry that around."
Rimu: "I'll have to tweak its appearance too, then."
Shimei: "It'll at least be able to stop someone temporarily, but..."
Rimu: "Goodness, you got out of that quick."
Shimei: "Well, all it really did was get caught on my leg."
Sakura: "What is with all the noise out here? We are trying to practice."
*I turn to the sound of the voice to find Toyama and Koume coming out of the dojo.*
Sakura: "You're distracting Koume. If you're going to be so noisy, do it somewhere else."
Koume: "I-I really didn't mind, though..."
Shimei: "No, we were definitely being noisy... I'm sorry we distracted you."
Rimu: "Oooh! Sakura-chan, Koume-chan! You showed up at just the right time!"
Sakura: "...Excuse me?"
Rimu: "Heheh... guess what! I've made a new device!"
Koume: "A new device?"
Rimu: "That's right. I'd like you two to try it out, if you would!"
Sakura: "Not a chance. If I had the time to waste on junk, I would rather read a book."
Rimu: "Oh-hoh, is that so? Are you really sure about that?"
Sakura: "...What are you trying to say?"
Rimu: "Apparently you aren't interested, so... Koume-chan, come check this out."
Koume: "O-Okay!"
Rimu: "You see, there's rope inside this box... That's right. And that thing there connects here..."
Koume: "W-Wow, amazing... I have never seen anything so complicated before."
Sakura: "......"
Rimu: "What's this? I thought you weren't interested, Sakura-chan."
Sakura: "Hmph! L-Like I'd be interested in that contraption!"
Shimei: "Geez, you just can't admit it, can you? Come take a closer look if you're that curious."
Sakura: "N-Not a chance! I have something to do. I'll be taking my leave!"
Rimu: "Aww... She left."
Koume: "D-Did I upset Sakura-oneesama somehow?"
Shimei: "Oh no, Toyama didn't leave because she was mad at you."
Koume: "I hope that is the case..."
Rimu: "D-Don't worry about it! Anyway, you should come up to my room, Koume-chan!"
Koume: "Eh? Up to your room, Rimu-neesama?"
Rimu: "I'll tell you all about how my machine works! Come on, let's go!"
Koume: "W-Wah! Please don't pull so hard!"
*Koume heads up to the second floor with Rimu practically dragging her along.*
Shimei: (Rimu certainly hasn't changed...)
*Rimu seems to be doing her best to include Koume, who's been having a hard time fitting in.*
*Now then...*
Shimei: (Time to go discuss some things with Hijikata...)
Shimei: "Hijikata, that was a pretty jerky move you made back there... Huh?"
*I thought Hijikata must have run off to the living room, but he isn't here.*
Shimei: "Is he hiding somewhere or something?"
*I speak out loud on purpose, but get no response.*
Shimei: "That's strange..."
Yamanami: "If you're looking for Hijikata, he just left a little while ago."
Shimei: "Erk! Y-Yamanami-san?!"
*I didn't notice her presence in the slightest.*
Yamanami: "He mentioned something about going out on patrol. Quite the workaholic even on a holiday."
Shimei: "Y-Yes, he is indeed."
*He'd really go that far to get away from Rimu and her machines...?*
Yamanami: "Are you free at the moment, Shimei-kun?"
Shimei: "I don't really have any particular plans today, so you could say that."
Yamanami: "Would you mind if I asked you to run an errand?"
Shimei: "An errand? I don't really mind, no."
*Even though I'm supposed to be showing Koume how to spend her day off, Rimu is far better suited to that task.*
*Best to just leave it to Rimu.*
Yamanami: "I have some business to attend to this evening, so I won't be able to make dinner."
Shimei: "So you want me to buy something for dinner?"
Yamanami: "How clever you are. Now then, I would like you to get us something from Tasuke Sushi."
Shimei: "Tasuke Sushi? That's just across Akabashi Bridge, right?"
Yamanami: "Correct. It's the sushi cart being run by an old man wearing a headband."
Shimei: "What kind of sushi should I buy?"
Yamanami: "Anything will do. I'll leave it all up to you, Shimei-kun. Here is the money you will need."
Shimei: "All right then, I will be on my way."
Yamanami: "Don't stay out too late, now!"
*As I step onto the main road, I spot Tojo-san and Saotome-san playing their usual game of street shogi.*
Tojo: "Hey there, novice magistrate. Must be nice to be so carefree that you can walk around by yourself in the middle of the day like this."
Shimei: "Today just happens to be a day off for me. I'm not like you with a lot of free time on my hands."
Tojo: "I stand corrected. So, would you like to play a round with me?"
*Ever since I met him, Tojo-san challenges me to a match every time he catches me free.*
*We've been pretty evenly matched so far, though I suspect he's been going easy on me.*
Shimei: "I have things I need to do today, so I can't play for long."
Tojo: "That's totally fine. Saotome, give him your spot."
Saotome: "Of course. Ooka-sama, here you are."
Shimei: "Thank you very much, Saotome-san."
Saotome: "No need to thank me."
Tojo: "You can have the first move, as usual, Ooka-kun."
Shimei: "If you insist."
*Starting with a standard opening move, I slide my pawn to 7F to open up a diagonal path for my bishop.*
Tojo: "So, what is this other task you need to do today that you mentioned?"
*Tojo-san's pawn goes to 3D. I want to avoid trading bishops with him.*
Shimei: "I need to go buy sushi for dinner tonight from Tasuke Sushi, just across Akabashi."
*I move my pawn to 7E, and Tojo-san moves his to 3E... avoiding an early confrontation.*
Tojo: "Ah, Tasuke Sushi? That place is great. Cheap and tasty."
Shimei: "You're familiar with it?"
*I'll have to use my special third file rook move here, my rook to 7H.*
*Tojo-san counters with his rook to 3B. Now we're even.*
Tojo: "Of course I am. I know more about Oukacho than you do, Ooka-kun."
*The smug look of self-satisfaction in Tojo-san's eyes pierces straight through me.*
Saotome: "Ooka-sama, this is the only thing he can boast about. Please forgive his impertinence."
Shimei: "That won't be necessary... I am completely unfazed."
*Even cheap sushi is still sushi, expensive by ordinary standards... Are these two better off than I thought?*
*I move my king to 4H. He follows with his king to 6B.*
Tojo: "Unfazed? I don't like the sound of that. You're making me sound like a real pity case, here."
*Continuing with my gold general to 5H, his gold general to 5B. Despite being second in turn, he uses a Mino castle defense as a counter-attack.*
Tojo: "It's about time for our pieces to clash, don't you think?"
*He seems awfully confident... or is he just underestimating me?*
Shimei: "I figured you would try to trick me somehow, Tojo-san."
*That was most likely a bluff to test me. I move my rook to 7F, his rook goes to 3D... and now I'm sure.*
Tojo: "So what's your next move, Ooka-kun?"
*Tojo-san is intentionally copying all of my movements so that we'll eventually clash.*
Shimei: "...I will be the one to attack, then."
*Victory will be assured for the first attacker... I advance my pawn to 7D, coming into contact with his front line.*
Tojo: "That's it. You have to come at me confidently like that."
*His silver general to 8B. I move a pawn to 7C and promote it, but he takes it with his silver general.*
Tojo: "Come on now, don't be so quiet. You should talk while you play, otherwise shogi is a gloomy game."
Shimei: "U-Ummm... Right, let's see..."
Tojo: "You seem rather distracted. You sure you can handle being magistrate of Nakamachi?"
Shimei: "I am doing my best."
*I'm not very good at playing shogi and holding a conversation at the same time.*
*Which is probably also part of Tojo-san's strategy...*
Tojo: "You must really have a handle on things if you have the spare time to play shogi with me like this."
Saotome: "Ooka-sama, this man has no understanding of what it means to be a town magistrate. Please forgive him."
Shimei: "It does not bother me. I believe the fact that I can take time off is proof things are peaceful."
Tojo: "Oh? Then I guess when you're busy, it's a tip-off that something's wrong."
Shimei: "Not necessarily. Nakamachi was originally created to alleviate the burden on Minamimachi and Kitamachi."
Shimei: "And even when everything is going smoothly, we still have to process mountains of paperwork."
Tojo: "So you're saying it's normal for you to be busy anyway?"
Shimei: "Yes, I am indeed."
Tojo: "So busy you've stopped playing, I see. What's your next move going to be?"
Shimei: "Oh, yes... Let me think."
*I drop a pawn on 7D, and again his silver general takes it.*
Tojo: "Can't think about two things at once, can you?"
Shimei: "Figured me out, have you?"
Tojo: "Yeah, I have. Your thoughts are written all over your face, Ooka-kun."
Shimei: "I don't know what it is, but when it gets close to the brinkmate I just lose all focus."
Tojo: "Why don't you just try to relax and play?"
Tojo: "When you get like this, you stop making anything except textbook-standard moves."
Shimei: "Well, I do understand that... in theory."
Tojo: "Standard moves are important, sure. But you don't wanna get stuck relying on them every time."
Tojo: "You need to be more open-minded. You'll find you get further that way."
Tojo: "Just like me!"
Saotome: "Ooka-sama, this man is a playboy. Please just take his words as nonsense from a commoner."
Shimei: "N-No... You don't need to make excuses for him."
Tojo: "Ah, that's right. I forget that I'm speaking with the town magistrate when I'm with you."
Shimei: "My apologies. I'm not very good at speaking with dignity."
Tojo: "I'm not one to talk, but I think that's better than the usual pompous government official."
Saotome: "I completely agree. Fostering a familiar and friendly atmosphere is very valuable."
Shimei: "I'm glad to hear you say so."
Saotome: "But please, as town magistrate, take care not to allow people to make light of you."
Saotome: "This man, at the very least, is taking you much too lightly, Ooka-sama."
Shimei: "Haha... Well, I guess that's not surprising."
Saotome: "Forgive me, I have said too much."
Tojo: "Why don't we go back to focusing on the game, Ooka-kun. If you win this match, then I'll tell you a secret of mine."
Shimei: "Your secret?"
Tojo: "Indeed. Feel a little more motivated now? Saotome, you come up with something too."
Saotome: "Me as well? All right then. I will give you information that will be beneficial to you, Ooka-sama."
Shimei: "And if I were to lose?"
Tojo: "Nothing needs to happen. Now then, novice magistrate, how are you going to get out of this situation?"
*Tojo-san's secret?*
*It probably isn't anything of great consequence, but the way he phrased it piques my interest.*
*Of course, it's probably also part of his plan to distract me.*
*However, given the circumstances, I can't just play as I always do.*
*It's time to try something drastic...*
Tojo: "Well now... Things have gotten more interesting."
Tojo: "...I lost."
Shimei: "Thank you for the game."
*In a rather surprising turn of events, I managed to win an easy victory by playing more instinctively.*
*But, somehow, I'm left with the inescapable feeling that I was led to win.*
Tojo: "How did it feel to move more freely?"
Shimei: "So you were leading me to win, weren't you? I knew I won that far too easily."
Tojo: "Ah well, what's the harm? We can have a real match next time."
Saotome: "Tojo-sama, since you lost the match, please tell Ooka-sama one of your secrets."
Tojo: "You're right. The truth is, I was once a swordsmanship instructor to the Shinsengumi."
Shimei: "You were?!"
Tojo: "I know I don't look it. It was quite a long time ago."
Tojo: "The young folks in there now probably wouldn't know me, but however I look, this old man is still tough."
Saotome: "By which you mean to justify your rudeness towards Ooka-sama as well, I suppose."
Tojo: "Erk... You know, you don't have to be so harsh."
*I have a hard time believing that Tojo-san was the Shinsengumi's instructor... which, knowing Tojo-san, might be the right response.*
*It could be a joke to justify his attitude, like Saotome-san says.*
Saotome: "I also have information to give you, Ooka-sama. Are you familiar with Koshikakean, on the main street?"
Shimei: "Yes, I am, but I've only heard the name and have never been there."
*Koshikakean is one of the sweet shops that Rimu likes to frequent.*
*She's invited me to join her there numerous times, but the timing never works out and I've never gone.*
Saotome: "The sweets there are particularly good. If you were to buy some as a treat to take back with you, it would make any woman or child exceedingly happy."
Saotome: "If there is a young woman you have your eye on, then by all means, please go there. It will turn out very well."
Shimei: "Y-You don't say..."
Saotome: "I believe most women would like it. That is it for my secret."
*You call that a secret?*
Tojo: "Which only means you would like it, doesn't it?"
Saotome: "So what if it does? Do you take issue with that?"
Tojo: "I-I don't. I have no problem with that. None at all."
Saotome: "You sure about that?"
Tojo: "Absolutely. I concede."
Saotome: "Thank you."
*I'm much more curious about the relationship between the two of them than anything else, but...*
Tojo: "Well, we've got stuff to do, so we'll get going. Thanks for the match."
Saotome: "Thank you very much for helping Tojo-sama kill some time."
Shimei: "Oh no, the pleasure is all mine."
Tojo: "See ya. Make sure to hone your skills before our next match."
*Tojo-san and Saotome-san, in good spirits, disappear into the crowd of people on the main street.*
Shimei: "That was a nice way to kill time. I should probably get going to Tasuke Sushi now..."
Tasuke: "Welcome! What can I do for ya?"
*When I arrive at the stall, the enthusiastic voice of its owner, Tasuke Ookura-san, greets me.*
Shimei: "Hello. Umm, I would like to buy sushi for a large number of people... Hmm?"
*Just as I'm thinking about what sushi to buy, my gaze is drawn to a large, conspicuous signboard.*
*"Now offering tempura", it boasts in big letters.*
Shimei: "Tempura...?"
Tasuke: "What good taste you have, sir! Once you try our tempura you will be completely addicted."
Tasuke: "Would you like to try a bite?"
Shimei: "I'm not sure..."
*I've had freshly fried tempura several times before, and it was always excellent.*
*And the smell is so enticing... After expending all my mental energy during that shogi match earlier, it's making me even hungrier.*
Tasuke: "Holding back isn't good for ya, sir."
Shimei: "It will get all soggy if I take it back with me..."
